I’m not sure about the following:

1. Whether adding the getManager method to terminusManager will be accepted.
2. Whether moving startSensorPolling to post PDR init or changing the original
```
for (const auto& tid : addedTids)
```
to perform startSensorPolling on all termini to achieve the same effect is better.

If there is a more suitable approach, I would appreciate any suggestions.
Thank you very much.

startSensorPolling() [1] is called after `afterDiscoverTerminus`.
The `afterDiscoverTerminus()` [2] will call `platformManager.initTerminus` which getPDRs from the EP. The functions are coroutine function current code is already make sure that `startSensorPolling` is called after get the PRDs from terminus. 
[1] https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/fb732fd99648eae137a1606a702906b2aa5b4756/platform-mc/terminus_manager.cpp#L196

[2] https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/fb732fd99648eae137a1606a702906b2aa5b4756/platform-mc/manager.cpp#L19

Under normal circumstances, the behavior is as you described.
However, there's a specific scenario where this issue arises.

Example:
If EID 20 is probed, the process begins by handling EID 20[1].
After finishing the terminus initialization, it attempts to get the PDR for EID 20 via initTerminus.
If a GetPDR error occurs during this step[2], the terminus->initialized = true flag is not set.
As a result, when startPolling is triggered, there are no sensors to poll[3], and EID 20's MctpInfos is removed from the queue.

Then, if EID 30 is probed, the process begins handling EID 30.
After initializing the terminus, it proceeds to initTerminus.
Since [4] retrieves PDRs for all terminuses, it will attempt to reinitialize EID 20's terminus because its terminus->initialized is set to false at this point. Consequently, GetPDR is performed for EID 20 first, and then for EID 30.
However, when PLDM returns to discoverMctpTerminusTask, [5] only calls startSensorPolling for addedTids, which in this case is EID 30.

This means that although EID 20 has successfully fetched the PDR this time and the PLDM tree is updated correctly, the PLDM does not initiate sensor polling for EID 20.
This is why I suggest moving startSensorPolling to occur right after terminus->initialized = true, or alternatively, modifying the existing logic in [5] to call startSensorPolling for all terminuses instead of just addedTids.

References:
[1] https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/fb732fd99648eae137a1606a702906b2aa5b4756/platform-mc/terminus_manager.cpp#L166
[2] https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/fb732fd99648eae137a1606a702906b2aa5b4756/platform-mc/platform_manager.cpp#L63
[3] https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/fb732fd99648eae137a1606a702906b2aa5b4756/platform-mc/sensor_manager.cpp#L47

[5]

So, should we avoid getting PDR for all terminus[4] during initTerminus, or should we release the successfully initialized termini when get PDR fails?
However, wouldn’t this make the terminus->initialized flag ineffective?

Thank you very much for your advice.

> So, should we avoid getting PDR for all terminus[4] during initTerminus,

The `platform-manager` will discovery the new MCTP EPs in `initTerminus ` one by one. The number of termini is initialized depend on the number added termini. I don't see any problem with this behavior.
 
> or should we release the successfully initialized termini when get PDR fails?

In the current code, each terminus has one `initialized` flag and this flag will be set to true when the discovery steps for that terminus is completed.

> However, wouldn’t this make the terminus->initialized flag ineffective?

Can you describe more about your idea in the `ineffective`?. 

> 
> Thank you very much for your advice.

> The platform-manager will discovery the new MCTP EPs in initTerminus one by one. The number of termini is initialized depend on the number added termini. I don't see any problem with this behavior.

My understanding is that each time `queuedMctpInfos` receives `addedTids`, the following steps occur:

1. The `initMctpTerminus` function initializes the `addedTids` into `termini`.
2. The `initTerminus` function then initializes the PDRs of all `termini` where `terminus->initialized` is false.
3. Finally, sensor polling is started for all `addedTids`.

However, since `initTerminus` processes all `termini` rather than only the `addedTids`, if a Tid encounters a `get PDR failed` scenario, the corresponding `terminus` for that Tid is not deleted and will still proceed to start sensor polling for that Tid.

When new `addedTids` are received next time, both `initMctpTerminus` and start sensor polling will only process the new `addedTids`.
However, during `initTerminus`, since it targets `termini` with `terminus->initialized` set to false, it will retry `get PDR` for the previously failed Tid. Even if the `get PDR` succeeds this time, sensor polling will still not be started for that Tid.

We have observed this issue multiple times in our system's journal logs.
This commit aims to prevent this situation, and after applying the patch, we have confirmed that the issue no longer reproduces.

> Can you describe more about your idea in the `ineffective`?. 

Regarding the idea that the `terminus->initialized` flag is ineffective:
If, as you mentioned, `initTerminus` should be modified to process only the `addedTids` instead of all `termini` with `terminus->initialized` set to false, it would imply there would no longer be any `termini` with `terminus->initialized` set to false. 
This is why I believe the `terminus->initialized` flag becomes ineffective in this scenario.

If there’s any part of my understanding that is incorrect, I would greatly appreciate your guidance.
Thank you very much for your patience and support!
